text.p: Following are the main stories in Thursday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The government has ordered national sewerage concessionaire Indah Water Konsortium Sdn Bhd to suspend indefinitely its billing and collection of charges with effect from Nov. 1. The government is reviewing the sewerage charges.

- Business leaders from the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) region have called for "concrete and measurable" actions that will result in a significant and tangible improvement in the business environment as well as benefits to the community at large.

- The inaugural Asem Business Forum between Asian and European businessmen in Paris on October 14 was a non-event and a complete disappointment, Technology Resources Industries Bhd chairman and chief executive Tajudin Ramli says.
- Two German nationals in a Cessna-172 made an emergency landing on the North-South Expressway near Slim River on Wednesday.

- Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the income distribution of the lowest 10 percent household has increased from 1.23 percent in 1979 to 1.7 percent last year and during the period, the income distribution for the top 10 percent has reduced from 38.7 percent to 36.6 percent.
